items.text: Quasi-separated reduces to quasi-compact (diagonal); coherent = both.
Correction: reduce to $Y$ affine; then $Y'$ is only quasi-compact (not affine); $X'$ quasi-compact and $X'\to X$ surjective $\Rightarrow$ $X$ quasi-compact.
Descent of finiteness properties
$g\colon S'\to S$ faithfully flat and quasi-compact: $f$ locally of finite type (locally of finite presentation) $\iff$ $f'$ is; hence finite type, finite presentation likewise.
Reduce: $S=Y$ affine; replace $Y'$ by a finite disjoint sum $Y''$ of affines (flat, surjective, quasi-compact); $X$ affine. Affine case:
A\to A'\ \text{faithfully flat},\ B\ \text{an }A\text{-algebra}:\quad B\ \text{of finite type (presentation) over }A\iff B'=B\otimes_AA'\ \text{over }A'
Finite type: $B=\varinjlim B_i$ ($B_i$ of finite type), $B'=\varinjlim B_i'$; if $B'$ is of finite type then $B'_i=B'$, hence $B_i=B$.
\text{Finite presentation: }B=C/J,\ C\ \text{polynomial ring; }B'=C'/J'\ \text{with }J'\ \text{of finite type}\Rightarrow J\ \text{of finite type (descent for modules)}
Modules: quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ is of finite type (finite presentation) iff $\mathcal F'$ is; $M=L/R$, $M'=L'/R'$ with $R'$ of finite type.
$\mathcal F$ locally free of finite type (of rank $n$; invertible) iff $\mathcal F'$ is.
\mathcal F\ \text{flat}\iff\mathcal F'\ \text{flat}\quad(g\ \text{faithfully flat, quasi-compactness not needed})
Proof: $N\hookrightarrow N_1$ injective; $M\otimes N\to M\otimes N_1$ is injective after $\otimes A'$ since $A'$ is flat and $M'$ is flat over $A'$. Faithful flatness descends too.
Locally free = finite presentation + flat, so descends; so does the rank.
Descent of topological properties
$g\colon S'\to S$, $Z\subset S$: always $\overline{g^{-1}Z}\subset g^{-1}\overline Z$; equality for all $Z$ $\iff$ $g$ open.
g\ \text{flat},\ f\colon Z\to S\ \text{quasi-compact}\ \Longrightarrow\ g^{-1}\bigl(\overline{f(Z)}\bigr)=\overline{g^{-1}(f(Z))}
Reduce to $S=\overline{f(Z)}$: i.e. $f$ dominating $\Rightarrow$ $f'$ dominating (the converse when $g$ is surjective).
Affine proof: $A$ reduced, $A\to B$ injective, $A'$ flat $\Rightarrow$ $A'\to B'$ injective.
Topological proof, $g$ only generalizing: lemma for $f$ quasi-compact,
f\ \text{dominating}\iff\text{the fibre over every maximal point of }S\ \text{is non-empty}
Proof: affine, $A$ reduced, $A\subset B$; residue fields at maximal points are $A_{\mathfrak p}$ ($\mathfrak p$ minimal); $A_{\mathfrak p}\subset B_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$.
A maximal point of $S'$ lies over a maximal point of $S$ (generalizing), and the fibre of $f'$ is the base change of a non-empty fibre.
Corollaries

$g$ flat and quasi-compact: the topology of $g(S')$ is the quotient topology of $S'$; $g$ faithfully flat and quasi-compact: the topology of $S$ is a quotient of that of $S'$ (universally submersive).
Proof: $Z\subset S'$ closed and saturated: $\overline{g(Z)}\cap g(S')=g(Z)$, since $Z\to S'\to S$ is quasi-compact.
$g$ quasi-compact faithfully flat: $f$ open, closed, generalizing, homeomorphism, (and their universal versions) descend from $f'$ to $f$.
Open: $g^{-1}(f(U))=f'(U')$ is open and $Y$ has the quotient topology. Closed: same.
Injective: a fibre $Z$ over a field with $Z'$ empty or a point is empty or a point.
Generalizing: $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ surjective, and $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ surjective.
$f$ separated $\iff$ $f'$ separated ($\Delta_f$ closed); $f$ proper $\iff$ $f'$ proper.
